title: VisuallyHidden
summary: Text for TalkBack only is set on the element itself with semantics properties. There is no hidden node, and Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: To name an icon-only control (contentDescription), to add context a sighted person gets from the layout, to replace several texts with one spoken phrase (clearAndSetSemantics), or to hide a decorative image (contentDescription = null).
whenNotToUse: Do not hide information from sighted people that TalkBack users get, or the reverse; if the context matters, show it. Do not replace visible text with a description that does not start with the visible words, which Voice Access uses to find the control.
api: fun Modifier.semantics(mergeDescendants: Boolean = false, properties: SemanticsPropertyReceiver.() -> Unit): Modifier
appearance: Nothing is drawn: the text exists only in the accessibility tree.
platformNotes: The web hides a span off screen so a screen reader still finds it in the document. Android has no document: each composable can carry semantics properties, so the spoken text is set on the element. contentDescription names it, stateDescription describes its state, clearAndSetSemantics replaces what its children would say with one phrase, and hideFromAccessibility() or a null contentDescription hides decoration. iOS uses accessibilityLabel, accessibilityValue and accessibilityHidden in the same way.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack reads contentDescription in place of an element's text, then its state description, then its role.
clearAndSetSemantics removes the children's semantics, so their actions must be set again on the parent if they are needed.
An Image or Icon with a null contentDescription is skipped by TalkBack.
edgeCases: Setting contentDescription on a node that merges its children replaces the children's text as well; use stateDescription to add to it instead.

examples.title: Screen-reader-only text
examples.template:
MonarchButton(
    text = {{visible}},
    onClick = {},
    modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = {{visible}} + " " + {{hidden}} },
    variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary,
)
examples.code:
MonarchButton(
    text = "Save",
    onClick = {},
    modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "Save" + " " + "changes to the ticket" },
    variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Secondary,
)
